words: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts earlier peoples who opposed the messengers and denied truth, and what befell them as punishment and chastisement.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن الأمم الماضين، وما حل بهم من العذاب والنكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bad consequence was the worldly punishment and humiliation brought by their denial and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: أي: وخيم تكذيبهم ورديء أفعالهم، وهو ما حل بهم في الدنيا من العقوبة والخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A painful punishment in the afterlife is added to the punishment they already suffered in this world.
rows.anchor: أي: في الدار الآخرة مضاف إلى هذا الدنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers came with clear proofs, evidences, and demonstrations.
rows.anchor: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات} أي: بالحجج والدلائل والبراهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought it implausible that messengership would belong to human beings and that a person like them could guide them.
rows.anchor: أي: استبعدوا أن تكون الرسالة في البشر، وأن يكون هداهم على يدي بشر مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the truth and turned away from acting upon it.
rows.anchor: أي: كذبوا بالحق ونكلوا عن العمل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had no need of them; He is self-sufficient and praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: أي: عنهم {والله غني حميد}

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali glosses protecting yourselves and your families from the Fire as disciplining and teaching them.
rows.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه، في قوله تعالى: {قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا} يقول: أدبوهم، علموهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to obey God, avoid disobedience, and command one's family to remember God, by which God saves them from the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا} يقول: اعملوا بطاعة الله، واتقوا معاصي الله،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the command as fearing God and advising one's family to fear God.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا} قال: اتقوا الله، وأوصوا أهليكم بتقوى الله.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says to command obedience, forbid disobedience, uphold God's commands, assist the family in them, and restrain and rebuke them when they sin.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يأمرهم بطاعة الله، وينهاهم عن معصية الله، وأن يقوم عليهم بأمر الله،

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil say a Muslim must teach family members, including relatives and enslaved people, the duties God imposed and the acts He prohibited.
rows.anchor: وهكذا قال الضحاك ومقاتل: حق على المسلم أن يعلم أهله، من قرابته وإمائه وعبيده،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report commands teaching children prayer at seven and striking them for neglecting it at ten; al-Tirmidhi grades this wording hasan.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مروا الصبي بالصلاة إذا بلغ سبع سنين، فإذا بلغ

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Dawud also transmits through Amr ibn Shuayb, from his father and grandfather, a prophetic report giving the same instruction about children's prayer.
rows.anchor: من حديث عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists extend the training principle to fasting so children reach maturity accustomed to worship, obedience, avoiding sin, and leaving wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال الفقهاء: وهكذا في الصوم؛ ليكون ذلك تمرينا له على العبادة، لكي يبلغ وهو مستمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fuel is the firewood cast into the Fire: the bodies of human beings.
rows.anchor: {وقودها} أي: حطبها الذي يلقى فيها جثث بني آدم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the stones as the idols people worshipped, citing the statement that worshippers and what they worship besides God are fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: {والحجارة} قيل: المراد بذلك الأصنام التي كانت تعبد لقوله:

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد وأبو جعفر الباقر والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Mujahid, Abu Jafar al-Baqir, and al-Suddi identify the stones as sulfur stones.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ومجاهد وأبو جعفر الباقر، والسدي: هي حجارة من كبريت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid adds that the sulfur stones smell worse than carrion.
rows.anchor: زاد مجاهد: أنتن من الجيفة.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report Ibn Abi Hatim calls mursal and gharīb, an elderly companion asks whether Hell's stones resemble earthly stones; the Prophet swears one rock of Hell is greater than all the world's mountains. The man faints, revives, professes God's oneness, and is promised Paradise; the Prophet confirms this and cites God's warning.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي نفسي بيده، لصخرة من صخر جهنم أعظم من جبال الدنيا كلها".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers have harsh natures because mercy toward those who disbelieve in God has been removed from their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي: طباعهم غليظة، قد نزعت من قلوبهم الرحمة بالكافرين بالله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their constitution is extremely strong and dense, and their appearance is frightening.
rows.anchor: أي: تركيبهم في غاية الشدة والكثافة والمنظر المزعج.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima describes 400,000 dark-faced, merciless keepers at Hell's first gate, followed by nineteen keepers of immense size; the gates are separated by five hundred years of descent, and each later gate has keepers like those at the first.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه قال: إذا وصل أول أهل النار إلى النار، وجدوا على الباب أربعمائة ألف من خزنة جهنم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels promptly carry out every divine command without even a moment's delay and are fully able to do it.
rows.anchor: أي: مهما أمرهم به تعالى يبادروا إليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These angels are the Zabaniya, the keepers of Hell from whom refuge is sought.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء هم الزبانية عياذا بالله منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the disbelievers are told not to offer excuses because they will not be accepted; they will be repaid for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي: يقال للكفرة يوم القيامة: لا تعتذروا فإنه لا يقبل منكم، وإنما تجزون اليوم بأعمالكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere, resolute repentance erases earlier sins, repairs and gathers the repentant person's scattered affairs, and restrains them from low conduct.
rows.anchor: أي: توبة صادقة جازمة، تمحو ما قبلها من السيئات وتلم شعث التائب وتجمعه، وتكفه عما كان يتعاطاه من الدناءات.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar, reported through al-Numan ibn Bashir and Sammak ibn Harb, defines it as sinning and then not returning to the sin; the reports repeat this definition in similar wording.
rows.anchor: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه، يقول: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا} قال: يذنب الذنب ثم لا يرجع فيه.

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud says that one repents and then does not return to the sin.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله: {توبة نصوحا} قال: يتوب ثم لا يعود.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet defines repentance from sin as repenting of it and not returning to it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "التوبة من الذنب أن يتوب منه، ثم لا يعود فيه".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the marfu report through Ibrahim al-Hijri is weak and that the mawquf version is sounder.
rows.anchor: من طريق إبراهيم بن مسلم الهجري، وهو ضعيف، والموقوف أصح

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars require leaving the sin now, regretting past wrongdoing, resolving not to repeat it, and restoring any right owed to another person.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال العلماء: التوبة النصوح هو أن يقلع عن الذنب في الحاضر، ويندم على ما سلف منه في الماضي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir refers back to his discussion of the disconnected letters at the start of al-Baqara, saying Nun is like Sad and Qaf and that the earlier treatment makes repetition unnecessary.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم الكلام على حروف الهجاء في أول "سورة البقرة"، وأن قوله: {ن} كقوله: {ص} {ق}

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes Nun to be a huge whale in the vast surrounding current, bearing the seven earths.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بقوله: {ن} حوت عظيم على تيار الماء العظيم المحيط،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, God first creates the Pen and commands it to write destiny through the Day of Resurrection; He then creates Nun, raises water vapor from it to form the sky, and spreads the earth on its back. When Nun moves, mountains fix the earth.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم قال: اكتب. قال: وما أكتب؟ قال: اكتب القدر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second Ibn Abbas version says God first created the Pen, which wrote all things until the Resurrection, then created Nun above the water and compressed the earth onto it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الضحى، عن ابن عباس قال: إن أول شيء خلق ربي، عز وجل، القلم، ثم قال له: اكتب.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a marfu report from Ibn Abbas that God first created the Pen and the whale, told the Pen to write everything until the Resurrection, and identified Nun as the whale and the Pen as the Pen.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن أول ما خلق الله القلم والحوت، قال للقلم: اكتب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says God first created the Pen and then Nun, identified here as an inkpot; the Pen wrote deeds, livelihood, traces, and lifespans until the Resurrection, was sealed, and was followed by the creation of the intellect.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن أول شيء خلقه الله القلم، ثم خلق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports the view that Nun is the great fish beneath the seventh earth.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كان يقال: النون: الحوت [العظيم]

rows.speaker: البغوي وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi and other commentators say a rock as thick as the heavens and earth rests on the whale, a bull with forty thousand horns rests on that rock, and the seven earths lie on the bull; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وذكر البغوي وجماعة من المفسرين: إن على ظهر هذا الحوت صخرة سمكها كغلظ السموات والأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls it strange that some commentators apply this cosmological whale story to the authentic report that Paradise's first food is an extra portion of a whale's liver.
rows.anchor: ومن العجيب (7) أن بعضهم حمل على هذا المعنى الحديث الذي رواه الإمام أحمد:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report of Abdullah ibn Salam's questions, the Prophet says the first sign of the Hour is a fire driving people from east to west, the first food of Paradise is extra whale liver, and a child's resemblance follows whichever parent's fluid prevails; the report is in al-Bukhari and Muslim.
rows.anchor: عن أنس: أن عبد الله بن سلام بلغه مقدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، فأتاه فسأله عن أشياء،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Muslim's report from Thawban, a rabbi asks about Paradise's welcome gift and food and drink: the Prophet answers extra whale liver, a bull of Paradise, then water from a spring called Salsabil.
rows.anchor: عن ثوبان: أن حبرا سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن مسائل، فكان منها أن قال: فما تحفتهم؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A mursal, gharīb report says Nun and the Pen are a tablet of light and a Pen of light that writes what will happen until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} لوح من نور، وقلم من نور،

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says he was informed that the luminous Pen is one hundred years long.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج (4) أخبرت أن ذلك القلم من نور طوله مائة عام.

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify Nun as an inkpot, while the Pen is the writing implement.
rows.anchor: عن معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله: {ن} قالا هي الدواة.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A marfu report from Abu Hurayra says God created Nun, meaning the inkpot; Ibn Kathir calls this report very strange.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "خلق الله النون، وهي الدواة"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created the inkpot Nun and the Pen and ordered the Pen to record every deed, good or evil, and every lawful or unlawful provision, with each person's earthly course and lifespan. Angels copy each day's deeds from the record; after provision, traces, and lifespan end, they find the person has died and no further deeds remain on the register.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله خلق النون -وهي الدواة-وخلق القلم، فقال: اكتب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas argues that the Arabic verb for copying means transcription from an original, using the angels' statement that they copied people's deeds.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ألستم قوما عربا تسمعون الحفظة يقولون: {إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is the generic writing pen, as in the passage about God teaching by the Pen.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه جنس القلم الذي يكتب به كقوله {اقرأ وربك الأكرم الذي علم بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the Pen and calls attention to the blessing of teaching writing, through which knowledge is acquired.
rows.anchor: فهو قسم منه تعالى، وتنبيه لخلقه على ما أنعم به عليهم من تعليم الكتابة التي بها تنال العلوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada gloss the phrase as what people write.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: يعني: وما يكتبون.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas instead glosses it as what people do.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الضحى، عن ابن عباس: {وما يسطرون} أي: وما يعملون.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase refers to angels and what they write down of people's deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {وما يسطرون} يعني الملائكة وما تكتب من أعمال العباد.

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view identifies the Pen as the one God used to record the decrees fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل المراد هاهنا بالقلم الذي أجراه الله بالقدر حين كتب مقادير الخلائق

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports the Prophet saying the Pen was God's first creation and was ordered to write destiny, past and future forever; Ibn Kathir notes Ahmad's multiple routes and al-Tirmidhi's grading of hasan, sahih, gharīb.
rows.anchor: دعاني أبي حين حضره الموت فقال: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A separate report from Ibn Abbas says the Pen was the first thing created and wrote everything; Ibn Kathir calls this route gharīb and says the compilers did not transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أنه كان يحدث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أول شيء خلقه الله القلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Pen is the one used to write al-Dhikr.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {والقلم} يعني: الذي كتب به الذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reiterates that the phrase means what they write.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وما يسطرون} أي: يكتبون كما تقدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not mad, despite the ignorant people among his nation who denied the guidance and manifest truth he brought and called him mad.
rows.anchor: أي: لست، ولله الحمد، بمجنون، كما قد يقوله الجهلة من قومك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has immense, unending reward for conveying God's message and enduring his people's abuse; Ibn Kathir explains ghayr mamnun as uncut, like the reward in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: أي: غير مقطوع كقوله: {عطاء غير مجذوذ}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses ghayr mamnun as uncounted; Ibn Kathir says this returns to his explanation that the reward is unending.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {غير ممنون} أي: غير محسوب، وهو يرجع إلى ما قلناه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو مالك والسدي والربيع بن أنس والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, al-Rabi ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd interpret the Prophet's great character as his great religion, Islam.
rows.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: أي: وإنك لعلى دين (1) عظيم، وهو الإسلام.

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya interprets the phrase as referring to great manners.
rows.anchor: وقال عطية: لعلى أدب عظيم.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In reports through Qatada and Sa'd ibn Hisham, and through Zurarah ibn Awfa, Aisha answers that the Prophet's character was the Quran; Ibn Kathir says Muslim records the long report and will revisit it in al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: سئلت عائشة عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. قالت: كان خلقه القرآن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha cites this verse about the Prophet's character, then recounts that she had a servant spill Hafsa's food when it arrived first; the platter broke, and the Prophet calmly gathered it and ordered a replacement vessel without rebuke.
rows.anchor: فقالت: أما تقرأ القرآن: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم}

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In another report through Sa'd ibn Hisham, Aisha says the Prophet's character was the Quran; Ibn Kathir notes a similar report through al-Hasan in Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i.
rows.anchor: عن سعد (2) بن هشام: قال: أتيت عائشة أم المؤمنين فقلت لها: أخبريني بخلق النبي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Nufayr reports that after he entered upon Aisha during pilgrimage and asked about the Prophet's character, she again said it was the Quran; Ahmad and al-Nasa'i also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن جبير بن نفير قال: حججت فدخلت على عائشة، رضي الله عنها، فسألتها عن خلق رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet made the Quran's commands and prohibitions his settled character, doing what it commands and avoiding what it forbids, alongside God-given modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, forbearance, and every fine trait.
rows.anchor: ومعنى هذا أنه، عليه السلام، صار امتثال القرآن، أمرا ونهيا، سجية له، وخلقا تطبعه،

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says that during ten years of service the Prophet never said even uff, never asked why he did or failed to do something, had the best character, the softest hand, and the sweetest scent; Ibn Kathir cites the report in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين عن أنس قال: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports that the Prophet was the best in appearance and character, neither exceptionally tall nor short; al-Bukhari transmits the report.
rows.anchor: سمعت البراء يقول: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن الناس وجها، وأحسن الناس خلقا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that many reports describe the Prophet's character and points to al-Tirmidhi's book al-Shama'il.
rows.anchor: والأحاديث في هذا كثيرة، ولأبي عيسى الترمذي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet never struck a servant, woman, or anything with his hand except while fighting in God's path; when offered two choices he chose the easier unless it was sinful, and he never avenged personal wrongs but acted when God's sanctities were violated.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما ضرب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده خادما له قط، ولا امرأة،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying he was sent only to perfect noble character; Ahmad transmits it uniquely by this route.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إنما بعثت لأتمم صالح الأخلاق". تفرد به
